compiled_state.description:
## Context
AWS account 896586841071, us-east-1: `rebar-root-disk-pressure` changed OK→ALARM at 2026-08-17 21:51:56 PDT and ALARM→OK at 22:12:56 PDT on the `rebar-gerrit` host (`i-00880b2c7f13527c5`, 30-GiB gp3 root `vol-0270fcf13709cf472`). Root usage climbed from 71% at 20:55 through the 85% alarm floor to 90% at 21:55/22:00, then dropped abruptly to 48% at 22:05. The review-bot health metric dipped to 0 at 22:05 while Gerrit remained healthy; `deploy_deferrals` emitted 2/3/1 at 21:55/22:00/22:05, with zero `voter_errors` and `deploy_errors`. Both SNS state actions succeeded.

This is the first recurrence after commit 32992f2b6c / closed story `sour-plugugly-rhino`, whose stated intent was to prevent `root-disk-pressure` by pruning Docker caches on pressure during no-op deploy ticks. Recovery was automatic and much faster than the prior 39-hour incident, but the alarm still breached and the review bot became briefly unhealthy, so prevention/headroom remains incomplete.

## Phase 1 status
Root cause is not yet proven. Read-only AWS evidence rules out an AWS Run Command/operator cleanup and shows an on-host reclaim aligned with the 90%→48% drop. Two leading, discriminating hypotheses remain:

1. Snapshot GC defaults to pruning only below 2 GiB free (~93.3% used on this disk), later than the CloudWatch alarm floor of ~4.5 GiB free (85%), so review snapshot churn can page before GC acts.
2. Autodeploy prunes Docker caches after successful build or on a deployed no-op tick, leaving pending/deferred/build windows able to cross the alarm threshold before reclaim.

Bounded host journald and disk-consumer evidence is required to distinguish Docker/build cache from review snapshots or another consumer before repair.

## Plan
- Capture bounded, read-only host evidence for the incident window and/or a safe local reproduction to identify which bytes grew and what reclaimed them.
- Form falsifiable hypotheses from that evidence and prove the dominant mechanism dynamically before changing code.
- Build a RED oracle at the smallest tier crossing the proven growth/reclaim path, then repair under held-out RED→GREEN and exact-defect mutation.
- Ensure reclaim occurs before the 85% alarm floor on every reachable growth path, with hysteresis, while preserving tagged rollback images, live/grace snapshot entries, and fail-safe behavior.
- Verify Gerrit/review-bot remain healthy and update the operations/config documentation for the selected mechanism.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Bounded host evidence or a faithful local reproduction identifies the dominant disk consumer and the component responsible for the 90%→48% reclaim.
- [ ] A discriminating runtime experiment proves the root cause and rules out the surviving Docker-vs-snapshot alternative.
- [ ] A test is observed RED on the proven mechanism, GREEN after repair, and RED again under the exact-defect mutation.
- [ ] The repaired path reclaims with hysteresis before a 30-GiB root crosses the 85% alarm floor.
- [ ] Tagged rollback images and live/grace snapshot entries are preserved.
- [ ] Gerrit/review-bot health and existing fail-safe deploy/review semantics remain intact.
- [ ] Relevant runbook/config documentation and the final rebar-debug report are updated.
compiled_state.title: [root-disk-pressure] Root disk reaches 90% and review-bot drops unhealthy after automated-reclaim mitigation
